examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
B+ internal nodes guide searches while leaves store data entries and commonly link for range scans. Fanout depends on key/pointer sizes and node-layout overhead. 'Order' conventions vary, so use the supplied maximum children/keys definition. Splits may propagate upward and create a new root. Exact minimum occupancy depends on root exceptions and rounding. Search depth counts levels; I/O can be one less if the root is cached.

**Key relationship:** Internal capacity: p·pointerBytes+(p−1)·keyBytes ≤ pageBytes

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Read the order convention.
2. Compute fanout and leaf capacity separately.
3. Handle split propagation and root exceptions.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Track maximum keys and maximum child pointers separately: an internal node with k separator keys has k+1 children. On leaf split copy the new separator upward while retaining its data entry; an internal split generally promotes/removes a separator. Splits can propagate to the root and increase tree height.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A B+ tree internal node has 7 separator keys. How many child pointers does it have?

**Answer: 8.** Separators divide key space into one region before the first, six between keys, and one after the last: eight child intervals. Thus k keys require k+1=8 child pointers.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Minimum occupancy has a root exception. Split position conventions can differ; use the rule stated in the question when tracing exact keys.

Do not assume “order” always means maximum keys; use the question’s explicit convention.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

B+ tree leaf links primarily aid:

- **A.** Removing all index levels
- **B.** Preventing all splits
- **C.** Only hashing
- **D.** Ordered range scans

**Answer: D.** After locating the first key, linked leaves allow sequential traversal through the range.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Internal fanout depends on key/pointer sizes
- **B.** Root occupancy can have special rules
- **C.** Every insertion splits the root
- **D.** Leaf and internal layouts can differ

**Answer: A, B, D.** Splits occur only on overflow, and a root split requires propagation to the root.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Ignoring overhead, an internal node has 512 bytes, 8-byte pointers and 8-byte keys. Maximum children p if it has p pointers and p−1 keys?



**Answer: 32.** 8p+8(p−1)≤512 gives 16p≤520, hence integer p≤32.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2025 CS2 · Q57 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/b-plus-trees?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** B-trees and B+ trees. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Insert 23 into leaf C, giving [20,22,23,25,26]. Splitting the overfull leaf copies a new separator (23 or 25 according to the permitted leaf split) into B.
2. B then has five separators. Its middle separator is promoted, splitting it into left and right internal nodes. The new right internal node begins with 33, followed by 44.
3. The leaf containing 25 lies under that right node, whose smallest separator is **33**. Root A has room to accept the promoted separator.

#### GATE 2025 CS1 · Q21 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/b-plus-trees?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** B-trees and B+ trees. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Inserting 23 targets the rightmost leaf [20,21,22], already at its maximum of three keys. That leaf must split and send a separator to its parent.
2. The root already holds three keys and cannot accept the extra separator without splitting. A new root is required.
3. At least one node splits and the height increases; the node count also grows. Select **B,D**.
